graphicsUpgrades.what: Ocean PBR light response for High Seas — the ocean is currently emissive-only (colorNode near-black, roughness 1, whole look in emissiveNode) despite computing correct analytic Gerstner normals it never uses. Staged: (1) drop roughnessNode toward ~0.15 modulated by wave slope for genuine sun glints; (2) sample the per-arena sky backdrop as environment reflection; (3) SSR stays registry-gated for later.
graphicsUpgrades.payoff: The single biggest visual jump available — the sixth arena is mostly water and it currently has zero specular and zero reflections. Stage 1 is a pure material change with no new passes.
graphicsUpgrades.risk: Specular glints must stay below the bloom-threshold contract (>1.0 linear reserved for true emitters) or bright water washes out; testable against the CPU grade-chain reference. Buoyancy parity untouched — positionNode's vertical field is a literal CPU transcription and must not change.

graphicsUpgrades.what: PMREM each arena's existing equirect sky backdrop into scene.environment on the WebGPU path. IBL is currently WebGL-only (legacy-main constructs GraphicsRefinementSystem with softwareRenderer=true whenever backend==='webgpu', hitting the early return), so the per-arena environment-intensity table never applies on the showcase backend and 'reflectionQuality' works by RAISING roughness to remove reflections.
graphicsUpgrades.payoff: High — metallic surfaces (chopper, containers, weapon receivers) receive no ambient specular at all on WebGPU today. The sky textures and per-arena scales already exist; this wires them together.
graphicsUpgrades.risk: Keep the deliberately small per-arena scales so authored directional/practical lights remain the dominant modelling source (graphics-refinement.ts:37-49). Watch D3D12 pipeline-state compile pressure — more light-graph inputs means more PSO permutations (documented mitigation in light-occlusion.ts).

graphicsUpgrades.what: A real volumetric tier: TSL height-fog / half-res dithered raymarched light shafts as a new tier above the current point-sprite layers, or minimally lift the mote/layer caps on Max (volumetricScale is clamped to [0.35,1] so Ultra equals the authored baseline — zero headroom by construction). The HF-363 technique list already names the raymarch approach.
graphicsUpgrades.payoff: High on industrial-night Rustworks and High Seas sea-spray ambience — the cheapest 'modern' atmosphere win available; god rays currently exist only as authored geometry lobes.
graphicsUpgrades.risk: Fog density directly contests sightlines. Keep per-layer opacity caps (mist 0.12) and the 'every tier retains at least one layer' rule; density must be presentation-only and identical in gameplay effect across profiles.

graphicsUpgrades.what: Spatial AO denoise: add three r185's DenoiseNode after GTAO. Temporal filtering is pinned off with no substitute, so raw 8/12/16-sample AO at 0.35-0.75 resolution scale reaches the screen undenoised (the game samples gtaoPass.getTextureNode().r directly).
graphicsUpgrades.payoff: Removes AO speckle/banding, biggest on the Low preset (0.35 scale, 8 samples). Single-frame and compatible with the deterministic fixed-time review cameras.
graphicsUpgrades.risk: Low — but it must be the SPATIAL denoiser, not enabling temporal filtering: there is no history resolve/velocity MRT, and TAA-style ghosting behind moving enemies is a readability hazard. Note GTAO High previously failed the 15s arena-transition soak on the RTX 5080 — soak-test the added pass.

graphicsUpgrades.what: Soft shadow filtering tier: PCFSoft on WebGPU (three r185 ShadowNode supports it), optionally VSM for the farcrysis golden-hour sun, and a 4096 shadow-map tier on Max. Farcrysis already authors sun.shadow.radius=7 explicitly commented as requiring PCFSoftShadowMap — that softness is currently inert because only BasicShadowMap/PCFShadowMap are ever selected.
graphicsUpgrades.payoff: Soft penumbrae on the island arena (activating already-authored art direction), less shadow-acne shimmer on High Seas deck edges.
graphicsUpgrades.risk: Bounded — shadows are presentation-only and identical across peers; slightly blurred occupant silhouettes in shadow is the only readability consideration.

graphicsUpgrades.what: Contrast-adaptive sharpen stage on the WebGPU grade chain, placed display-referred before per-frame-luminance-grain. The WebGL2 path already sharpens (AtomicSignalPass 5-tap, 0.12) but the WebGPU chain has no sharpen stage at all — and renderScale goes down to 50% with no TAA/upscaler to restore edges.
graphicsUpgrades.payoff: Crisper image at sub-native render scale and look-parity between the two backends.
graphicsUpgrades.risk: The chain order is a fail-closed contract (assertGradeChainOrder throws) — a new stage means updating the frozen contract and its tests deliberately. Hard-clamp sharpen the same way grain is clamped so no halos land on high-contrast sightline edges.

graphicsUpgrades.what: A genuine bloom QUALITY tier (higher bloom-chain resolution / more mip levels on Max). bloomQuality currently maps only to strength (0/0.065/0.14); the BloomNode is built once at fixed low resolution with bloomSamples: 0.
graphicsUpgrades.payoff: Cleaner tight glows on real emitters (Rustworks practicals, tracers, High Seas beacons) at 1440p/4K instead of blocky halos. The depth-edge guard already prevents silhouette smearing.
graphicsUpgrades.risk: Low — threshold stays profile-owned and fail-closed above 1.0 linear (tuneBloomForProfile throws otherwise), so no wall can wash out a sightline regardless of tier.

graphicsUpgrades.what: MeshPhysicalNodeMaterial clearcoat on the chopper fuselage and operator visors, iridescence on visor glass. Physical materials currently exist only on building glass and debris shards; operators and vehicles normalize everything to MeshStandardMaterial.
graphicsUpgrades.payoff: Moderate — reads as 'next-gen' on close-up review cameras and killcams; per-material swaps fully compatible with the existing TSL pipeline audit.
graphicsUpgrades.risk: Shader-permutation compile time — this codebase is already sensitive to D3D12 PSO exhaustion. Gate to High/Max, prewarm via precompileExactScenePass, and preserve tslPipelineId tags.

graphicsUpgrades.what: Velocity MRT attachment as enabling INFRASTRUCTURE (the scene pass MRT carries only output+normal today). Not user-visible itself, but it is the single documented blocker behind GTAO temporal filtering, SSR occlusion receipts, DoF and motion blur.
graphicsUpgrades.payoff: Indirect — unlocks the entire next tier of gated effects with one piece of plumbing.
graphicsUpgrades.risk: Keep motion blur off by default in a competitive FPS (reduced-motion contract is mandatory); do not expose any gated control until its documented gates pass — the inventory generator audits that unavailable rows allocate zero GPU resources.
